summary: Miami beat Pittsburgh 52-23 behind Toney’s record receiving day. Protection, coverage and red-zone execution lead the review before the road trip to North Carolina.

items.headline: Miami beats Pittsburgh 52-23
items.tldr: The Hurricanes stayed unbeaten with another productive offensive outing. Carry the scoring plan forward while checking the protection and defensive plays hidden by the margin.

items.headline: Toney sets Miami’s single-game record with 16 catches
items.tldr: He finished with 194 receiving yards and three touchdowns. Watch the space created before the catch and the block that helps the next gain continue.

items.headline: Pass protection remains a concern after the win
items.tldr: State of The U flags pressure reaching Mensah despite the large margin. Match the quarterback’s release and receiving outlet to the protection before the next road test.

items.headline: Film review points to downfield coverage work
items.tldr: Pittsburgh still found long receiving plays. Keep the route in front of the safety help and finish the tackle instead of letting a completion become another open-field problem.

items.headline: Miami scores on all seven red-zone trips against Pitt
items.tldr: The official review counts six touchdowns and a field goal. Watch whether the offense keeps creating a usable first option as the field narrows.

lead.headline: Keep the clean throw available.
lead.body: Give the quarterback time and a receiving answer before asking the play to stretch. Carry that patience to the secondary, where leverage and a finished tackle must survive the first route break.

matchup.thesis: Make the protection match the route
matchup.question: What should fans watch in the next game?
matchup.answer: Keep an immediate outlet available when the defense sends pressure. Take the space underneath, then choose the deeper throw when the blocking and coverage create a real opening.

signals.title: Pass protection
signals.detail: Watch how long the route asks the line to hold and where the quick outlet appears. Keep the quarterback from waiting through another hitch without an answer.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with pass protection?

signals.title: Receiving space
signals.detail: Watch the receiver’s release, the nearby block and the defender’s leverage. Create a clean catch before expecting the runner to turn it into a long gain.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with receiving space?

signals.title: Secondary leverage
signals.detail: Keep the safety’s help connected to the receiver’s path. Close on the catch under control so one missed tackle does not erase the coverage work.

signals.title: Red-zone execution
signals.detail: Create space with the formation and route timing. Take the available score rather than letting a stalled first read turn into a desperate late throw.
